function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of the most prominent vaccine manufacturers around the world (as of 2026). These companies are responsible for developing, producing, and distributing vaccines for a wide range of diseases—from COVID‑19 and influenza to HPV, meningitis, and beyond.

| # | Company | Headquarters | Notable Vaccines | Key Highlights |
|---|---------|--------------|------------------|----------------|
| 1 | **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | New York, USA / Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 (Comirnaty) – COVID‑19; Prevnar 23 (pneumococcal) | First mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine; strong partnership with BioNTech; expanding mRNA platform to other diseases. |
| 2 | **Moderna** | Cambridge, USA | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – COVID‑19; RSV vaccine (under development) | Pioneer in mRNA technology; rapid vaccine development; strong pipeline for RSV, influenza, and oncology. |
| 3 | **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | New Brunswick, USA | Ad26.COV2.S (Janssen COVID‑19) | Single‑dose adenovirus‑vector vaccine; also produces vaccines for meningitis, HPV, and influenza. |
| 4 | **AstraZeneca** | Cambridge, UK | ChAdOx1 nCoV‑19 (Vaxzevria) – COVID‑19; Cervarix (HPV) | Global distribution network; partnership with Oxford University; focuses on low‑cost vaccines for LMICs. |
| 5 | **Novavax** | Gaithersburg, USA | NVX-CoV2373 (Nuvaxovid) – COVID‑19; RSV vaccine (under development) | Protein subunit platform; high efficacy; strong presence in emerging markets. |
| 6 | **Sanofi Pasteur** | Lyon, France | Fluzone (influenza), Menactra (meningitis), Prevnar 13 (pneumococcal) | One of the largest vaccine producers; extensive global supply chain; active in vaccine research for emerging pathogens. |
| 7 | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Vaccines** | Brentford, UK | Engerix‑B (HBV), Shingrix (shingles), Menveo (meningitis) | Strong focus on immunology; invests heavily in next‑generation vaccine platforms. |
| 8 | **Merck & Co. (MSD)** | Kenilworth, USA | Gardasil 9 (HPV), RotaTeq (rotavirus), Fluzone Quadrivalent | Global presence; diversified portfolio across viral and bacterial pathogens. |
| 9 | **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin (COVID‑19) | Indigenous vaccine platform; significant role in India’s vaccine supply; expanding into other vaccines. |
|10 | **Sinovac Biotech** | Beijing, China | CoronaVac (COVID‑19) | Inactivated virus platform; large domestic market; active in global vaccine diplomacy. |
|11 | **Sinopharm (China National Pharmaceutical Group)** | Beijing, China | BBIBP‑CorV (COVID‑19) | Inactivated vaccine; extensive domestic distribution; partnerships with WHO. |
|12 | **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany | CVnCoV (COVID‑19) | Non‑modified mRNA platform; exploring new vaccine candidates for influenza and RSV. |
|13 | **Takeda Pharmaceutical** | Tokyo, Japan | Takeda’s influenza vaccine (Fluad) | Strong presence in Asia; invests in influenza and enteric disease vaccines. |
|14 | **Biontech (BioNTech)** | Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 (COVID‑19) | Co‑founder of Pfizer‑BioNTech; focuses on mRNA therapeutics beyond vaccines. |
|15 | **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Covishield (AstraZeneca‑Oxford) | Largest vaccine manufacturer by volume; produces vaccines for polio, measles, and more. |

### How to Use This List

- **Research & Development**: If you’re looking into vaccine R&D, focus on companies with strong pipeline programs (e.g., Moderna, Novavax, CureVac).
- **Supply Chain & Procurement**: For bulk vaccine procurement, consider manufacturers with robust global distribution (e.g., Sanofi Pasteur, GSK, Merck).
- **Emerging Markets**: Bharat Biotech, Serum Institute, and Sinovac are key players in low‑ and middle‑income countries.
- **Technology Platforms**: mRNA (Pfizer‑BioNTech, Moderna, CureVac), adenovirus‑vector (Janssen, AstraZeneca), protein subunit (Novavax), and inactivated virus (Sinovac, Sinopharm).

If you need deeper details—such as current clinical trial status, manufacturing capacity, or partnership opportunities—just let me know!
